name: Grand piano (Steinway B)
note: An instrument recipe for the sampler (doc 24, Instruments, Sample preparation and Sampler rules). It describes exactly the files the prep step produced; nothing here is a tuning choice. type, id, name, version: what this is. source: where the recordings come from (library, folder url, license) and what the library's own note files say (notes). channels: channel count of every file. formats: each file exists once per format under root, as <file>.ogg (Ogg Opus, 48 kHz, 96 kbps stereo or 64 kbps mono, variable bitrate) and <file>.m4a (AAC-LC at the source rate, 128 kbps stereo or 96 kbps mono); the browser picks the first it can play. root: folder of the files, relative to the repo. layers: the number of velocity layers in the sustain set, layer 1 the quietest. sets: one entry per articulation: sus (sustain, pedal down or natural ring), nosus (dampers working), rel (release or key-off noise, played on note-off), pedal (sounds of the pedal mechanism). Each set has source (the library subfolder) and zones; a zone is one recorded key: note (scientific pitch, C4 = middle C, sharps written s in file names), midi (C4 = 60). measuredCents: the zone's measured pitch offset from 12-tone equal temperament at A4 = 440 Hz, in cents, as recorded; piano strings are inharmonic (partial n sits at n f0 sqrt(1 + B n^2)), so it is fitted from partials 1 to 6 (2 to 8 in the bass, where the fundamental is weak) over a window of the early sustain, each partial taken as the level-weighted centre of its unison-string cluster, and it is the pitch of the fitted first partial. Real pianos are stretch-tuned on purpose (bass flat, treble sharp); nothing has been corrected. tuneLayer: the layer the zone's number comes from (the middle one). tuneResidualCents: how far the found partials sit from the fit (root mean square, cents). tunePartials: which partials were found and used. layerSpreadCents: the largest difference between this zone's layers. inharmonicityB: the fitted B. unisonSplitCents: the widest spread seen inside one partial's cluster (a sign of unison strings tuned apart, which is heard as beating or chorus). tuneConfidence: 0 to 1, falls with fewer partials, a larger residual and a larger layer spread; below about 0.5 trust the ear over the number. layers: the files of the zone, quietest first; file is the path under root without extension; layer is its velocity layer and rr its round-robin take when the set has takes. peakDb: the file's sample peak in dBFS. attackRmsDb: the RMS level of its first 300 ms after the onset, in dBFS. Whether these levels mean anything depends on the source (see levels below). brightness: the share of energy above 1.5 times the note's fundamental (or 1 kHz, whichever is higher) in those first 300 ms, which should rise from layer to layer; in a very quiet file the noise floor can inflate it. lenS: length after the prep, in seconds. trimStartMs: how much was cut from the start (the onset, the first point above -50 dB of the file's peak, is kept with 3 ms before it). measuredCents on a layer is that file's own measurement. src: the original file name. Every file was cut where its 50 ms RMS fell to 60 dB below its peak, or at a maximum length (8 s at A0 falling evenly per semitone to 4 s at C8 for sustains, 2 s for releases), whichever came first, then given an equal-power fade over its last 250 ms (100 ms for releases and pedal sounds) so it ends in true silence. No gain was changed. levels: whether the source normalised each file (normalized true: the levels say nothing about how hard the key was played, so the sampler rebuilds the dynamic range from velocity with its own curve and must not re-gain the layers) or kept the recorded levels (normalized false: the layers already step up in level as they were played, and the sampler should play them at their own level). range: the lowest and highest sustain zone. problems: anything odd found while preparing, in plain words. The .m4a files decode about 23 ms longer than the .ogg files because AAC pads its last frame with silence; the start is in the same place in both. Steinway B: rel has a release sample per layer for most zones; a zone without one should fall back to the nearest zone's release.

source.notes: Folder 'Grand Piano, Steinway B', close mic, recorded by JH (files JHPiano_*). Subfolders: Sus (sustain pedal held down while recording), NoSus (dampers working normally), Rel (the release noise of the NoSus notes, files named NoSusRel). Velocity layers in the source are vl2, vl3 and vl4 (there is no vl1); here they are renumbered v1, v2, v3, quietest first. One round robin (rr1) only, so file names carry no rr. NORMALIZED.txt says: the sustain and no-sustain articulations were normalised; use a velocity curve to rebuild dynamic range and do not adjust the gain of layers or they will not line up. We followed it: no gain change, levels measured and recorded. The release set is not normalised (its peaks sit 30 to 64 dB below full scale) and keeps its recorded level. Note names in the files are standard scientific pitch (A#0 is the second-lowest A-sharp of the keyboard, C4 middle C), confirmed by pitch measurement.

levels.note: Sus and NoSus were normalised per file by the library (peaks -0.2 to -12 dBFS); rebuild dynamics with a velocity curve and never re-gain layers. Rel keeps its recorded level (peaks -29 to -64 dBFS).

problems: Steinway rel has no release samples from E6 up. That is expected: the top strings of a grand have no dampers, so there is nothing to release.
nosus: brightness does not rise with layer in 3 of 42 zones: Fs6 (v1 0.001, v2 0.000, v3 0.003); E7 (v1 0.000, v2 0.000, v3 0.000); Fs7 (v1 0.000, v2 0.000, v3 0.000)

sus: layers of the same key disagree in pitch by more than 5 cents in 1 zones (usually a high, fast-dying note or a unison that beats; the zone number uses the middle layer): Gs7 (v1 +6.0, v2 +5.6, v3 +20.6)

nosus: layers of the same key disagree in pitch by more than 5 cents in 5 zones (usually a high, fast-dying note or a unison that beats; the zone number uses the middle layer): Fs6 (v1 +6.7, v2 -0.9, v3 -0.7); As6 (v1 +6.2, v2 -2.4, v3 +1.7); C7 (v1 +16.4, v2 +9.2, v3 +8.9); D7 (v1 +17.8, v2 +9.5, v3 +10.4); Fs7 (v1 +18.3, v2 +10.2, v3 +9.1)
rel: no release sample for 9 sus zones: E6, Fs6, Gs6, As6, C7, D7, E7, Fs7, Gs7
